extracted.intended_audience: young married women, wives, and household managers seeking practical domestic and marital advice
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance and normative standards for married life focused on household management, the family purse, and interpersonal conduct between spouses. Advises wives (and husbands) on economy, division of money, domestic labor, housekeeping method, hospitality, and marital forbearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure men in context (avoid feminine standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: The surest guard against the shock of broken ideals is to keep ever before the mind that men are not to be measured by feminine standards of perfection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put John in his proper place as regards distances, shadow and environment, and survey him in the cool white light of common sense. Avoid 'canonizing' men; do not construe strength into coarseness or slowness into brutal indifference. Unless he is a poseur, he will appear best thus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept conjugal bickering as ordinary, not catastrophic
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugal quarrels are so constantly the theme of ridicule ... we lose sight of the plain truth that husbands and wives bicker no more than parents and children, brothers and sisters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat occasional clashes and passing heat of temper as 'surface-gusts' that do not stir brooding love. Wars come from infirmities of mortal nature, not matrimony per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion about a husband's faults
rubrics_metrics.description: While John remains loyal to his wedded wife ... the inventory of his faults should be a sealed book to her closest confidante; the carping discussion of his failings be prohibited by pride, affection and right taste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid public or prolonged carping; adopt pride, affection and good taste in withholding or tempering criticism of a spouse. Learn forbearance with offensive peculiarities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value husband's reticence and honor
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps the noblest reticence belongs to the Silent Side of him. He has a nicer sense of honor in commenting upon his wife's shortcomings than she exhibits with regard to his.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect his unwillingness to display yearning for sympathy publicly; use his example to learn discretion and forbearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual understanding about ownership of family income
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The crying need of a mutual understanding with respect to the right ownership of the family income.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear, mutual agreement on who owns and controls family funds is the most prolific source of preventing heart-burnings, contentions, and secret unhappiness among married people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the wife's domestic labor as paid work (salary, not gratuity)
rubrics_metrics.description: He who keeps house, manages servants, bears and brings up his children ... does not consider that his wife has paid her way thus far, and is richly entitled to all he has given or will ever give her— is not fit to conduct any business upon business principles. If he be sensible and candid, let him decide what salary he can afford to pay this most useful of his employés—and pay it as a debt, and not a gratuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat domestic duties as employment: estimate a fair salary for the wife's services; pay a stated sum rather than ad hoc 'gifts' to avoid humiliation of dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a stated household allowance plus a personal discretionary sum to the wife
rubrics_metrics.description: She ought to have a stated allowance for household expenses ... and a smaller, but sure sum which is paid to her as her very own, which she may appropriate as she likes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disburse household funds for expenses and also give the wife a separate, personal fund to spend at her discretion; avoid models where husband 'gives' money as charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not render the wife pauper by absorbing her fortune into husband's business
rubrics_metrics.description: The wife whose handsome wedding portion has been absorbed by her husband's business is as dependent upon his favor for her 'keep' as she who brought no dot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect the wife's independent interest in her portion; recognize absorption of her fortune into husband's affairs creates unfair dependence and resentment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Husband should be transparent and enlist wife's sympathy in long-term financial plans
rubrics_metrics.description: If he can enlist her sympathies in his plans for earning independence and wealth, he has secured a valuable coadjutor. If he can show her that he is investing certain moneys which are due to her ... he will retain her confidence with her respect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share investment plans and evidence of prudent use of funds to maintain trust; treat wife as partner in financial strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Women should be allowed to own property in their own right
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of us likes to own something in his or her own right. The custom ... that make wives the solitary exception to the rule that the 'laborer is worthy of his hire,' are unworthy of a progressive age.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable wives to hold accounts/possessions in their own name; such independence is not likely to alienate a sensible husband and is progressive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid living beyond means with ostentatious houses and insufficient help
rubrics_metrics.description: By keeping up a certain appearance of affluence, they assume the obligation to employ servants enough to carry out the design, yet in nine hundred and ninety-nine times out of every thousand, they ignore the duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not buy houses or furnishings beyond actual capacity to maintain them; if you adopt a showy standard, you must either employ adequate servants or simplify. Houses should be planned for those who live in them, not for fleeting visitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan homes for practical living (simplicity and congruity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire social and domestic system of American communities calls loudly for the reform of simplicity and congruity. Our homes should be planned and kept for those who are to live in them, not for those who tarry within the doors for a night or an hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design houses and domestic arrangements to suit daily life and inhabitants' capacities rather than appearances; avoid unfinished or impractical structures that burden householders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-ambitious housewifery; employ adequate domestic help where needed
rubrics_metrics.description: American women, from high to low, keep house too hard because too ambitiously. ... It is, furthermore, ambition without knowledge; hence, misdirected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when hiring help is sensible—mechanic's wife may correctly hire charwoman sometimes; pride should not force excessive personal labor leading to ill health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be realistic about costs overlooked in 'keep house on X' literature
rubrics_metrics.description: The authors of these books leave too many things out of the question. The expenses of moving and the purchase of necessary furniture are, of course, omitted, but Mary finds to her chagrin that fuel ... and light ... have not been taken into account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When budgeting, include fuel, lighting, moving costs, periodic cleaning help, and laundry; test rules against actual experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gain practical housekeeping experience before running your own home
rubrics_metrics.description: All the rules and theories ... are worth little compared with three months of personal experience. Happy is the young wife who has had some practice in housekeeping in her father's house before the heavier responsibility of a home of her own rests on her shoulders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apprentice in actual household work early to learn realistic management and avoid despair when facing a household of your own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy is not meanness; avoid waste
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no meanness in economy, and ... waste is vulgar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserve usable leftovers (butter scraps, cold potatoes, teaspoonfuls of cream) and use them resourcefully; small economies add up and are respectable, not shameful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mistress's direct involvement in cooking yields better economy and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: To utilize the little 'left-overs,' then, Mary must make up her mind to do much of her own cooking. ... If the mistress will spend half an hour in the kitchen before each meal, John will soon discover that his food has a delicacy of flavor ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lady doing some cooking improves flavor, reduces waste and breakage, and may be more efficient than hired cooks; delegate heavy work to servants but retain delicate tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit household staff; supervise servants closely if employed
rubrics_metrics.description: Every extra mouth counts, and the waste caused by each added Bridget or Gretchen is incalculable. The only redress ... is constant vigilance and personal supervision, and even then she is the loser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ as many servants as the household truly requires and can afford; if keeping servants, personally supervise provisions and supplies to avoid loss or theft; adapt practices regionally (e.g., locked provisions in the South may not work in the North).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wash one's own dining-room dishes to save money and reduce breakage
rubrics_metrics.description: Another of the petty economies ... is the washing of one's own dining-room dishes. The money saved by this process is easily understood ... The china bill for one year of the woman with many servants assumes proportions so huge ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With hot water, proper tools and care, dish-washing by the mistress is quicker, more thorough, reduces breakages, and yields satisfaction; the labor can be pleasant with the right setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospitality should not be counted out simply to save costs, but avoid pretentious entertaining
rubrics_metrics.description: I do not advocate ... pretentious entertaining ... But it impresses me that it is, to a certain extent, a mean spirit that counts the cost in asking a friend to stay to a repast ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep daily home so that occasional guests can be welcomed without major upheaval; explain modest living to guests and give them equal treatment without apology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematize household work—method is essential
rubrics_metrics.description: Some housewives are always in a hurry and their work is never done, while others with twice as much to do never seem flurried ... The secret of the success of the latter class lies in that one golden word--METHOD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize, schedule, and adopt methodical routines to save time and mental strain; method and management do wonders for saving time and money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress and garment choices should be practical for married life
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not discreditable to the sex to assert that a man is first attracted marriage-ward by the desire of the eye. ... In the work-a-day world of matrimonial life, much of all this undergoes a change ... white muslin comes to grief so speedily in the course of even light housework ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt clothing after marriage to practical domestic needs—choose fabrics and styles that tolerate household work and reduce laundry expense; do not persist in impractical fashion for daily duties.
